audits.mathematicalReason: Let F(x)=tan(2x)−cos(x/2). The excluded poles are π/4, 3π/4, 5π/4, and 7π/4, leaving five continuity branches. On each branch tangent increases while cos(x/2) decreases, so F strictly increases. Each of the three full interior branches runs from −∞ to +∞. On the first branch F(0)=−1 and the right-hand limit is +∞; on the last branch the left-hand limit is −∞ and F(2π)=1. Consequently each branch contains exactly one zero, for five solutions. audits.mathematicalReason: Dividing f by g leaves a remainder of degree at most two. It vanishes at three distinct roots, so it is zero and f(x)=(x+d)g(x). Comparing x coefficients gives 10+d=100, hence d=90; comparing x³ coefficients gives a+d=1, hence a=−89. Therefore f(1)=91·g(1)=91·(1−89+1+10)=−7007. The alternative extra-root calculation also works: if the fourth root is t, the triple-product identity gives −10+t=−100, so t=−90, and the root-sum identity then gives a=−89. Both routes fit their definitions.
